clue.text: Dieticians upset about pages revealing cause of abdominal pain

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and jumbled, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange
pp is the standard abbreviation for pages

explanation.surface: Nutritionists in a fluster over some pages that explain why someone has a stomach ache.
explanation.walkthrough: About tells you the pages sit inside the rearranged letters, here just after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the appendix is a classic medical reason for sharp pain low in the belly.

clue.text: Arouse tailless beast with time and energy

indicators.note: without a tail means the final letter of the creature word is dropped

blocks.note: an animal, losing its last letter
T is the usual abbreviation for time
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Waking up a creature that has lost its tail by giving it time and pep.
explanation.definitionFit: To animate someone is to stir them into life or excitement, a verb synonym for rousing them.

clue.text: Stagger up after exercise class with advanced high-protein snack?

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: PE is physical education, the school exercise lesson
A is a common abbreviation for advanced
to stagger someone is to stun them, read upwards here

explanation.surface: Someone tottering out of a gym class reaching for a protein-rich nibble.
explanation.walkthrough: The stagger word comes first in the clue but last in the answer: it sits after PE and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanuts are a protein-packed legume eaten by the handful as a bar or party nibble, hence the question mark for a definition by example.

clue.text: Troublesome individuals represented in a census

indicators.note: to be represented is to be shown in a new form, so the following letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A statistician's complaint that awkward people show up in the population count.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuisances are annoying people who cause bother, so they fit troublesome individuals as a plural noun.

clue.text: I swindle small people who are widely admired

blocks.note: taken as written
a con is a swindle
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A confession of cheating minor figures who are nonetheless much loved.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a celebrated figure revered as a symbol, so famous admired people are icons.

clue.text: I unusually retain resistance to change

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters come in an abnormal order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admitting they rarely keep anything, ironically while describing stubbornness.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics and in everyday use, inertia is the tendency of a body or person to stay as it is.

clue.text: Popular plant has circle in hell?

blocks.note: something popular is in
a fern is a plant
O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: A garden plant said to have a ring around it in the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: The circle also nods to Dante, whose Inferno divides hell into nine circles.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante named his vision of the underworld the Inferno, and the word now means any blazing hellish place.

clue.text: Believe fit to be great

blocks.note: to consider is to believe or judge
able means fit or capable

explanation.surface: Thinking someone is in good enough shape to be outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: A considerable amount is a large or significant one, matching great in the sense of size.

clue.text: Japanese art leaders of army museum kept in unfinished base

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so only the opening letters of the next words count
something unfinished lacks its end, so the final letter is dropped
kept in means held inside, so the first piece sits within the second

blocks.note: the first letters of these two words
a base or source is an origin, here missing its last letter

explanation.surface: A display of Japanese craft stored in the unfinished foundations of a military museum.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the traditional Japanese craft of folding paper into shapes.

clue.text: Past US agent given too much dough?

blocks.note: something past is over
a fed is an FBI agent in American slang

explanation.surface: A former American spy who was perhaps paid far too much money.
explanation.walkthrough: Dough looks like money for the agent, but it is bread dough, food, which is why the question mark is there.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone overfed has been given more food than needed, and dough playfully stands for bread to eat.

clue.text: Frustrated detectives given job

blocks.note: DIs are detective inspectors
someone appointed has been given a post

explanation.surface: Police investigators annoyed despite being handed a new assignment.
explanation.definitionFit: Being disappointed means feeling let down when hopes are thwarted, close to feeling frustrated.

clue.text: Cooking utensil ejected by posh lady, half-cut

indicators.note: cut in half means only one half of the word survives

blocks.note: spat is the past of spit, to eject from the mouth
U means upper-class in British usage
only the front half of this is kept

explanation.surface: A kitchen tool flung out by a tipsy upper-class woman; half-cut is British slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A spatula is a flat-bladed kitchen tool for lifting, spreading or scraping food.

clue.text: Skits based on Salvation Army fatigues

blocks.note: SA is the abbreviation for the Salvation Army
fatigues as a verb means tires

explanation.surface: Comic sketches inspired by military uniforms worn by the Salvation Army.
explanation.walkthrough: Fatigues looks like army clothing, but it is the verb meaning wears out.
explanation.definitionFit: Satires and skits are both short comic pieces that mock their subject.

clue.text: Doctor, for example, beginning to swallow sediment

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter only

blocks.note: Dr is the title abbreviation for doctor
e.g. abbreviates for example
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A medic illustrating how to start gulping down a murky residue.
explanation.definitionFit: Dregs are the gritty residue left at the bottom of a cup or bottle, a plural synonym for sediment.

clue.text: Very happy bird with a ring

blocks.note: a cock is a male bird
taken as written
a hoop is a ring

explanation.surface: A cheerful bird sporting a ring, like a ringed pigeon.
explanation.definitionFit: Cock-a-hoop is an old idiom for being jubilant or crowing with delight.

clue.text: Honour A-lister fee

blocks.note: an A-lister is a top celebrity, or celeb
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: Reads like a request to pay tribute to a star's appearance fee.
explanation.definitionFit: To celebrate someone is to honour them publicly with praise or festivities, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Tries again with a little bit of laborious practice

indicators.note: the smallest bit of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: to rehear a case in court is to try it again
taken as written
just the opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone making another attempt at a tiresome practice session.
explanation.walkthrough: Tries is the legal sense: a judge rehears a case. The a of the clue does double duty with the selector words, giving A before the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice run of a performance before the real thing.

clue.text: Crop top under hideous Afghan robe, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the first letters of the preceding words
in a down clue, under means placed below, so the garment word goes second, after the initials

blocks.note: the opening letters of these three words
a vest is a sleeveless top

explanation.surface: A fashion note about a short top worn beneath an ugly Afghan coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A harvest is the crop gathered in a season, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Adult with superior accessory

blocks.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
superior means better

explanation.surface: Reads like a fashion tip: a grown-up wearing a classier accessory.
explanation.definitionFit: In law an accessory is someone who helps commit a crime, which is what an abetter does.

clue.text: Some grapes topping sauce

indicators.note: some means only part of what follows, a run of letters inside the words

blocks.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A recipe idea: a few grapes scattered on top of a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian sauce of basil, pine nuts, garlic and cheese.

clue.text: More sprightly lord embracing queen, king and setter

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the noble wraps round the other letters

blocks.note: a peer is a lord
R for Regina, Latin for queen
K is the chess abbreviation for king
the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: A nobleman cheerfully hugging royalty and the puzzle's author.
explanation.definitionFit: Perkier is the comparative of perky, meaning livelier and more cheerful, matching more sprightly.

clue.text: Dog jumps up to grab panini in the middle

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up reads the word from bottom to top
the middle of a word is its central letters only
to grab is to seize and hold, so the reversed word holds the other piece

blocks.note: leaps are jumps, read upwards here
the two central letters of this six-letter word

explanation.surface: A hungry dog leaps up to snatch a toasted sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaniel is a breed of dog with long drooping ears.

clue.text: Quarrels stop intense desire returning before first thing on Sunday

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read backwards
the first thing of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: to bar is to stop
a yen is a strong longing
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A plea to end family rows driven by craving before Sunday morning.
explanation.walkthrough: Barney is British informal for a noisy row.
explanation.definitionFit: A barney is colloquial British English for a loud argument, so barneys are quarrels.

clue.text: Unfortunately sneaky about commercial

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word surrounds the second

blocks.note: sly means sneaky
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: A regretful remark about a devious advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadly and unfortunately are both sentence adverbs expressing regret about what follows.

clue.text: Snatch back first-class number for a good deal

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the backward direction

blocks.note: to snatch is to grab
A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as I
N is an abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Grabbing a top-quality item back because it is cheap.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a common label for first-rate; crosswords swap the digit 1 for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is something bought cheaply, so it is a good deal for the buyer.

clue.text: Chose Juliet for line to be removed

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter stands where another was

blocks.note: to elect is to choose
Juliet is J in the NATO alphabet
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A theatre director picking Juliet so a line can be cut from the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Ejected means thrown out or expelled, so it fits removed as a past participle.

clue.text: Idiotic square like one before

blocks.note: as means like
I is the Roman numeral one
nine is a square number, three squared

explanation.surface: Calling someone a foolish conformist, like a person ahead of them.
explanation.walkthrough: Square looks like a word for an uncool person, but it is a square number; before puts the other pieces in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means extremely foolish, from the Latin for donkey, so it is a synonym of idiotic.

clue.text: Bird chewed pretty morsel

indicators.note: chewed food is mashed up, so the letters that follow are mangled into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A bird nibbling at a dainty titbit.
explanation.definitionFit: The storm petrel, or stormy petrel, is a small seabird said to appear before bad weather.
